chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarakhsi, the jurist in Sarakhs, told us, saying: Abu Lubaid Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isra'il told us, saying: Saif ibn Harun al-Barjami told us, from Amr ibn Qais al-Mula'i, from Umayya ibn Yazid al-Qurashi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:

Whoever performs a sin or gives refuge to a sinner, upon him is the curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. Neither ransom nor disbursal will be accepted from him on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the sin? He said: The one who kills a soul for other than (the cause of) another soul, or mutilates for other than retaliation, or invents an innovation with other than a tradition, or seizes a prey of value. He said: Then it was said: What is the ransom, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Redemption. He said: Then it was said: What is the disbursal, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Repentance.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific sins and conditions under which ransom and repentance are not accepted on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* to elucidate the specific categories of 'sin' (hadath) and the conditions under which the divine curse becomes irrevocable. The text clarifies that 'ransom' (adl) refers to material compensation (fidya), while 'disbursal' (sarf) denotes spiritual repentance (tawbah), emphasizing that mere compensation or repentance may be insufficient if the core innovation or act remains unaddressed. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the precise definitions of legal and spiritual penalties within the context of the Prophet's teachings.
